selected_evidence.summary: Showed accept_redirects=1 (all/default) and accept_source_route: all=0, default=1 prior to hardening.

selected_evidence.requirement: No conflicting pre-existing persistent config for these settings
selected_evidence.summary: Confirmed existing sysctl.d files (e.g. 10-network-security.conf) and sysctl.conf had these directives commented out or unrelated, so the new file would take effect without conflict.

selected_evidence.requirement: Persistent disabling of ICMP redirect acceptance and source-routed packet acceptance for IPv4
selected_evidence.summary: Created /etc/sysctl.d/60-icmp-redirect-hardening.conf, applied via 'sysctl --system', and verified live values net.ipv4.conf.all/default.accept_redirects=0 and accept_source_route=0 immediately after.

selected_evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: healthy baseline (boot identity) before restart
selected_evidence.summary: Captured boot_id=37344ae4-6582-4c1f-ac5c-fcb32f67b968 and uptime baseline prior to reboot.

selected_evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
selected_evidence.summary: Backgrounded delayed reboot command returned pid acknowledgement immediately, before the node disconnected.

selected_evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: node actually restarted (unreachable during reboot)
selected_evidence.summary: Immediately following exec call timed out, confirming the node was down mid-reboot.

selected_evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: changed boot identity proving genuine restart
selected_evidence.summary: Post-recovery boot_id=d5be2f6d-874b-4cd1-8df5-5caeea968a55, differing from baseline, proving a real reboot occurred (not just a service bounce).

selected_evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: required configuration persisted and recovered after restart
selected_evidence.summary: Post-reboot check shows sysctl values still 0 for accept_redirects/accept_source_route (all/default) and the persistent config file /etc/sysctl.d/60-icmp-redirect-hardening.conf intact with correct contents.

# redirection. Some network environments, however, require that these
# Do not accept ICMP redirects (prevent MITM attacks)
#net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_redirects = 0
#net.ipv4.conf.default.accept_redirects = 0
# Accept ICMP redirects only for gateways listed in our default
# net.ipv4.conf.all.secure_redirects = 1
# Do not send ICMP redirects (we are not a router)
#net.ipv4.conf.all.send_redirects = 0

# Turn on Source Address Verification in all interfaces to
# prevent some spoofing attacks.
net.ipv4.conf.default.rp_filter=2
net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter=2

commands.command:
cat > /etc/sysctl.d/60-icmp-redirect-hardening.conf <<'ANTRIEB_EOF'
# Disable acceptance of ICMP redirects (IPv4) - prevent MITM route injection
net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_redirects = 0
net.ipv4.conf.default.accept_redirects = 0

# Disable acceptance of source-routed packets (IPv4)
net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_source_route = 0
net.ipv4.conf.default.accept_source_route = 0
ANTRIEB_EOF
cat /etc/sysctl.d/60-icmp-redirect-hardening.conf
